Exactly one of LST_Q_009's four options realises that assertion: 'A technical problem spoiled their plan'. The other three (applause showed it went well / the slides were the strongest part / the audience left before it had finished) are off-dimension or contradicted by it.

In Step 2C4 I then recorded LST_Q_010_OPTIONS_DO_NOT_LEAK_Q009=true - I checked the OPTIONS direction on CLIP_04 and never asked whether the STEM does the same thing, in the very pass that had just learned the stem direction next door. By my own recorded leak definition it counts.

BLOCKER.title: isActive defaults to true and no read path filters on status, so importing V2 would switch every learner onto it and then 500 the diagnostic endpoint
evidence: prisma/schema.prisma DiagnosticAssessment: isActive Boolean @default(true) and status DiagnosticAssessmentStatus @default(ACTIVE)

The schema's own comment says 'status is authoritative for learner-current'. grep for a read path filtering on status returns 0. Four read paths filter on isActive: true (diagnostic.service.ts:527, 599, 616, 706), and getCurrentAssessment orders by id desc.
So assessment.statusOnCreate='DRAFT' in the content draft has NO effect on serving, and the failure mode is OMITTING isActive, not setting it wrong.
BLOCKER.consequence2: Worse than mis-serving. getCurrentAssessment calls assertQuestionBank before returning. The mapper writes productive tasks as options: [] and correctIndex: -1; getQuestionMeta takes its Array.isArray branch and returns {values: [], questionType: 'MCQ'}, so each of the 4 productive rows trips both 'invalid options' (values.length < 2) and 'invalid correct index' (-1 < 0). assertQuestionBank throws InternalServerErrorException, so GET /diagnostic/current would 500 for EVERY learner in the product, not only V2 takers. Verified by reading validateQuestionBank at diagnostic.logic.ts:242-286 and getQuestionMeta at :136-166.
BLOCKER.whatIKnewAndWhatIMissed: My persistence contract section 7 item 9 does say 'Create the assessment as DRAFT / inactive and assert isActive = false', so the requirement was known. What is written nowhere: that isActive DEFAULTS TO TRUE, that DRAFT does nothing because no read path reads status, and consequence 2 at all - grep for validateQuestionBank or assertQuestionBank in my persistence contract returns 0.
acceptanceCriteria: the importer sets isActive: false explicitly in the same statement that creates the row, inside the same transaction as the questions
getCurrentAssessment and getLatestResult select on status = ACTIVE rather than isActive: true + id desc, or a single-active invariant is enforced in the database
an executable test proves that inserting a DRAFT V2 assessment leaves GET /diagnostic/current serving the V1 form and not throwing
the contract states the isActive default and the validateQuestionBank consequence

D4-012.title: No V2-compliant row shape can pass the live question-bank validator without persisting a CEFR level
D4-012.evidence: validateQuestionBank branches on meta.questionType. For OPEN_TEXT it requires meta.stableKey && meta.section && meta.construct && meta.intendedLevel, and getQuestionMeta populates intendedLevel ONLY when the raw value is one of ['A1','A2','B1','B2'] (diagnostic.logic.ts:157). For anything else it requires values.length >= 2 and 0 <= correctIndex < values.length, which no productive task can satisfy. V2 policy forbids persisting a CEFR code and both mapper functions hard-set intendedLevel: null by design. The schema's actual discriminator, the taskType column, is never read by getQuestionMeta.
D4-012.acceptance: validateQuestionBank and getQuestionMeta read the taskType/skillCode columns as the discriminator and do not require intendedLevel; a fixture of all 29 mapped V2 rows returns zero defects.

D4-013.title: The mapper's options: string[] discards every field the runtime reads from the options JSON
D4-013.evidence: getQuestionMeta's object branch is where section, passageText, audioUrl, stableKey, construct and activeInForm live. A plain string[] takes the array branch, which returns only {values, questionType: 'MCQ'}. Consequences: sanitizeQuestion returns audioUrl only when meta.section === 'LISTENING', so no audio would be served for the 10 Listening items - and the same undefined disables validateQuestionBank's 'missing listening audio' check, so the blueprint readiness requirement is silently unenforced. sanitizeQuestion derives passage text from meta.passageText, which the mapper never sets (it sets the passageId FK, which sanitizeQuestion never reads), so no passage text would be served for the 10 Reading items. And the submit guard filtering on section === 'SPEAKING' would never fire for V2.
D4-013.acceptance: either the mapper writes options as the object form carrying the metadata the runtime reads, or getQuestionMeta/sanitizeQuestion migrate to the dedicated V2 columns and the DiagnosticListeningClip relation; a test asserts a mapped Listening row yields a non-empty audio URL and a mapped Reading row yields its passage text.

D4-015.title: GAP-1 confirmed but incomplete
D4-015.detail: The reviewer confirms there is no stable authored identity on DiagnosticQuestion and that re-import idempotency is impossible with the current schema. It adds that my MAPPING_GAPS record is incomplete: passage identity and assessment identity need the same treatment, the clip cardinality problem is a distinct defect from identity, mediaDraftKey is misclassified as authoring metadata when it is a content reference needing a target, and the rubric table is already satisfied by @@unique([skill, rubricVersion]) and should be explicitly excluded.

runtimeFindings.failOpenDetail: I verified this and it is worse than I reported in Step 2C4. There are FIVE production call sites, not two: diagnostic.logic.ts:305 and diagnostic.service.ts:343, 823, 1048, 1096. At 1048 and 1096 perm is computed as `attemptId && !isOpen ? getAttemptQuestionPermutation(...) : undefined` - gated on an OPTIONAL client-supplied attemptId. When it is absent, isDiagnosticAnswerCorrect falls through to `return answer === question.correctIndex`, comparing a DISPLAY index against an AUTHORED index. My Step 2C4 claim that this was 'not a current bug - both live callers pass it' was wrong on both counts.
runtimeFindings.toResultDetail: toResult returns selectedOption (a display index) beside correctOption (an authored index) with no marker distinguishing them, and gates key and rationale disclosure only on status === 'COMPLETED', never reading resultState. So a PENDING_GRADING V2 attempt could disclose all 25 keys before grading completes. D4-017.
runtimeFindings.confidentialityConfirmed: sanitizeQuestion's 12-field allowlist contains neither correctIndex nor explanation. Independently confirmed.
runtimeFindings.OPTION_RATIONALE_IDENTITY_STABLE_UNDER_S: true for the mapper's own helper, NOT PROVEN for the runtime grader

permutationProofCriticism.detail: My 24-permutation grading test asserts perm[displayed] === correctIndex, which is a tautology about the permutation array - it never calls isDiagnosticAnswerCorrect. The rationale test exercises rationaleForDisplayedOption, which has no production caller. So ANSWER_KEY_STABLE_UNDER_SHUFFLE=true was proved about my own helper functions, not about the runtime. The actual runtime grader has 2-permutation coverage. This is the same failure mode I claimed to have structurally fixed: a narrow check reported under a broad flag name.
permutationProofCriticism.acceptance: a test drives isDiagnosticAnswerCorrect, and ideally the sanitizeQuestion -> submit round trip, across all 24 permutations with the authored key, including the {originalIndex} answer shape with a permutation supplied; the tautological test is deleted or renamed.
